references.text: The laws concerning Hebrew slaves and their release, including protection against being sold, demonstrate the same principle of human dignity and limitations on ownership over people.
The prohibition against human trafficking and the sale of Israelites reflects the same ban on selling a woman who has been taken as a wife.
The law regarding a man who has had sexual relations with a virgin and must then take responsibility for her illustrates the same principle of protecting women after sexual intercourse.
Sarai treated Hagar harshly, an example of mistreating a woman in a vulnerable position, which this law seeks to prevent.
Laws concerning the treatment of female slaves who have had sexual relations with a man show similar protections and restrictions.
The prophet Jeremiah warns against abusing and exploiting vulnerable people, which aligns with the prohibition against exploiting a freed woman.
